**Part (a): Determine the no-load speed ($N_{NL}$).**

The speed of a DC motor is proportional to the back EMF ($E_b$) and inversely proportional to the field flux ($\Phi$):
$$N \propto \frac{E_b}{\Phi}$$

The back EMF is given by:
$$E_b = V - I_a R_a$$
where $V$ is the supply voltage, $I_a$ is the armature current, and $R_a$ is the armature resistance.

**1. No-Load Condition (NL):**
$V = 230 \text{ V}$, $I_{a,NL} = 5 \text{ A}$, $R_a = 0.15 \text{ } \Omega$.
$$E_{b,NL} = 230 - (5)(0.15) = 230 - 0.75 = 229.25 \text{ V}$$
$$N_{NL} \propto \frac{229.25}{\Phi_{NL}}$$

**2. Full-Load Condition (FL):**
$V = 230 \text{ V}$, $I_{a,FL} = 50 \text{ A}$, $R_a = 0.15 \text{ } \Omega$.
$$E_{b,FL} = 230 - (50)(0.15) = 230 - 7.5 = 222.5 \text{ V}$$
The flux is reduced by 2% due to armature reaction:
$$\Phi_{FL} = \Phi_{NL} (1 - 0.02) = 0.98 \Phi_{NL}$$
$$N_{FL} = 1200 \text{ rpm}$$
$$N_{FL} \propto \frac{222.5}{0.98 \Phi_{NL}}$$

**3. Relating the speeds:**
$$\frac{N_{NL}}{N_{FL}} = \frac{E_{b,NL} / \Phi_{NL}}{E_{b,FL} / (0.98 \Phi_{NL})} = \frac{E_{b,NL}}{E_{b,FL}} \times 0.98$$
$$\frac{N_{NL}}{1200} = \frac{229.25}{222.5} \times 0.98$$
$$\frac{N_{NL}}{1200} \approx 1.029 \times 0.98 \approx 1.0084$$
$$N_{NL} = 1200 \times 1.0084 \approx 1210.08 \text{ rpm}$$

**Part (b): Starting conditions and external resistance.**

**1. Line Current at Standstill ($I_{L,start}$):**
At standstill, the motor acts as a simple resistive load.
The field current ($I_{sh}$) is determined by the shunt resistance ($R_{sh}$):
$$I_{sh} = \frac{V}{R_{sh}} = \frac{230 \text{ V}}{230 \text{ } \Omega} = 1 \text{ A}$$
The total line current is the sum of the armature current ($I_a$) and the shunt current ($I_{sh}$):
$$I_{L,start} = I_a + I_{sh}$$
The armature current at standstill is:
$$I_{a,start} = \frac{V}{R_a} = \frac{230 \text{ V}}{0.15 \text{ } \Omega} \approx 1533.33 \text{ A}$$
$$I_{L,start} = 1533.33 + 1 = 1534.33 \text{ A}$$

**2. External Resistance ($R_{ext}$):**
We want the starting current ($I_{a,start}'$) to be 125% of the full-load armature current ($I_{a,FL}$).
$$I_{a,FL} = \frac{P_{out}}{V I_{L,FL}}$$
First, find the full-load armature current ($I_{a,FL}$).
The rated line current is $I_{L,FL} = 56 \text{ A}$.
$$I_{a,FL} = I_{L,FL} - I_{sh} = 56 \text{ A} - 1 \text{ A} = 55 \text{ A}$$
The desired starting current is:
$$I_{a,start}' = 1.25 \times I_{a,FL} = 1.25 \times 55 \text{ A} = 68.75 \text{ A}$$
The total resistance in the armature circuit is $R_{total} = R_a + R_{ext}$.
We apply Ohm's law at starting:
$$I_{a,start}' = \frac{V}{R_a + R_{ext}}$$
$$68.75 = \frac{230}{0.15 + R_{ext}}$$
$$0.15 + R_{ext} = \frac{230}{68.75} \approx 3.345$$
$$R_{ext} = 3.345 - 0.15 = 3.195 \text{ } \Omega$$

**Conclusion:**
Part (a) result: $N_{NL} \approx 1210 \text{ rpm}$.
Part (b) results: $I_{L,start} \approx 1534 \text{ A}$, $R_{ext} \approx 3.2 \text{ } \Omega$.
